title: Job therapy and toxic coworkers, with Tessa West, PhD

sentences.en: Are you and your job just not clicking anymore?
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得你和你的工作再也无法契合了？

sentences.en: Maybe a toxic co-worker is making your life miserable, or maybe you're trying to figure out why you're not getting promoted, or why your workload is suddenly out of control.
sentences.zh: 也许是有毒的同事把你的生活搞得一团糟，也许是你一直在琢磨为什么自己总是得不到晋升，或者为什么你的工作量突然失去了控制。

sentences.en: Or perhaps you're wondering whether you're even in the right field.
sentences.zh: 或者，你可能在怀疑自己到底是不是选对了行业。

sentences.en: Maybe it's time to change not just jobs, but your career.
sentences.zh: 也许是时候不仅要换工作，还要改变你的职业生涯了。

sentences.en: Today, I'm going to talk to an expert in the science of work and workplace communication about how to handle tough career situations like these, and why improving communication
sentences.zh: 今天，我将与一位研究工作科学和职场沟通的专家探讨如何应对这些艰难的职业困境，以及为什么改善与同事、老板及其他人的沟通是找到成功且令人满意的职业的关键。

sentences.en: with your co-workers, bosses, and others is the key to finding a successful and satisfying career.
sentences.zh: 那么，当你的工作不适合你时，你该怎么办？

sentences.en: So what should you do when your job isn't working for you?
sentences.zh: 如果你正在考虑换工作或改行，你该如何弄清楚自己为什么对工作不满意，以及什么才是更好的选择？

sentences.en: If you're considering a job or career change, how can you figure out why you're dissatisfied with your work, and what could be a better fit?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能应付有毒的同事，或者一开始就避免和他们纠缠在一起？

sentences.en: How can you handle toxic co-workers, or avoid getting stuck with them in the first place?
sentences.zh: 总的来说，你如何才能找到能让你大展宏图的有意义的工作？

sentences.en: And overall, how can you find fulfilling work where you will thrive?
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学话你知》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学协会（American Psychological Association）的王牌播客，主要探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是纽约大学（New York University）心理学教授苔丝·韦斯特（Tessa West）博士。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Tessa West, a professor of psychology at New York University.
sentences.zh: 韦斯特博士研究许多场景下的为人际沟通科学，其中包括职场环境。

sentences.en: Dr. West studies the science of interpersonal communication in many contexts, including in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 她于7月出版的最新著作名为《工作疗法：寻找适合你的工作》（Job Therapy, Finding Work That Works For You）。

sentences.en: Her latest book, published in July, is called Job Therapy, Finding Work That Works For You.
sentences.zh: 而她于2022年出版的上一本书则是《职场混蛋：有毒的同事以及如何应对他们》（Jerks That Work, Toxic Coworkers and What to Do About Them）。

sentences.en: And her previous book, published in 2022, is Jerks That Work, Toxic Coworkers and What to Do About Them.
sentences.zh: 韦斯特博士的研究探讨了诸多问题，例如人与人之间的地位差异如何塑造他们的行为，为什么给出诚恳、批判性的反馈会如此困难，阶级、种族和文化差异如何使职场沟通变得困难，以及我们能做些什么来改善这种状况。

sentences.en: Dr. West's research has examined questions such as how status differences between people shape how they behave, why it's so hard to give honest, critical feedback, how class,
sentences.zh: 她发表了数十项研究，并获得了美国国家科学基金会（National Science Foundation）和美国国家卫生研究院（National Institutes of Health）的多项资助。

sentences.en: race, and cultural differences can make communication in the workplace difficult, and what can we do to improve it.
sentences.zh: 她的工作受到了各大媒体的报道，其中包括《科学美国人》（Scientific American）、《纽约时报》（The New York Times）和美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）等，这只是其中的几个例子。

sentences.en: She has published dozens of research studies and received multiple grants from the National
sentences.zh: 韦斯特博士，非常感谢你今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: Science Foundation and the National Institutes of Health.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来参加这个节目。

sentences.en: Her work has been covered by media outlets, including Scientific American, The New York
sentences.zh: 你的新书名叫《工作疗法》，但你自己是一位研究心理学家，而不是治疗师。

sentences.en: Times, and CNN, to name just a few.
sentences.zh: 为什么你觉得采用“疗法”这个框架是审视工作和职业问题的好方法？

sentences.en: Dr. West, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me on the show.
sentences.zh: 我其实是在研究亲密关系、研究浪漫关系以及我们与家庭成员、孩子和父母的关系的过程中，渐渐产生这个想法的。

sentences.en: Your new book is called Job Therapy, but you're a research psychologist yourself, not a therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 在工作的纽约大学，我教授一门关于亲密关系的课程大约有15年了，我开始发现人们谈论职场问题的方式与他们感受到的情绪之间有很多重叠之处，比如矛盾心理、同时爱着又痛恨着自己的工作等复杂情况，还有面试中的一些趋势，比如“幽灵隐身”（ghosting）、“冷落”（icing）之类的事情。

sentences.en: Why did you decide that framework of therapy was a good way to look at work and career issues?
sentences.zh: 这些同样的事情也是我一直在浪漫关系背景下教授的内容，并且是该领域的治疗师们长期以来一直在努力应对、帮助人们理清头绪的概念。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 我想，为什么不把其中一些治疗视角——那些我们知道能帮助人们度过人际关系困难的经验——应用到我们与职业的关系中呢？

sentences.en: I actually kind of came around to this idea, studying close relationships, studying romantic
sentences.zh: 现在，你在书中概述了导致人们考虑离职的五个关键驱动因素。

sentences.en: relationships and relationships we have with our family members, our children and our parents.
sentences.zh: 你能简要谈谈这些因素吗？

sentences.en: And at New York University, where I work, I've been teaching a course on close relationships for about 15 years, and I started to see a lot of overlap between the ways people were
sentences.zh: 可以，我其实是从最艰难、最本质的一种开始的，那就是在工作中经历身份危机。

sentences.en: talking about their workplace issues, the emotions that they were feeling, you know, complex things
sentences.zh: 这种想法指的是，你可能会对某个长期定义你身份的事物失去热情，你作为一个人内心深处对自己的核心认知——你作为人类的身份认同——与你的职场身份紧密相连，但你开始对此产生质疑。

sentences.en: like ambivalence, loving and hating your job at the same time, trends around interviewing, like ghosting and icing and these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 我认为经历这一过程的人通常在职业生涯中已经取得了很高的成就。

sentences.en: These same things were things that I've been teaching in the context of romantic relationships
sentences.zh: 他们为了走到这一步付出了大量的时间和金钱。

sentences.en: and concepts that therapists in that space have been grappling with for a really long time and helping people kind of get their head around.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有很高的地位。

sentences.en: And I thought, why not adopt some of those therapeutic perspectives, some of the things that we know
sentences.zh: 因此，努力去接受自己对一个依然定义着自己的事物失去热爱，是我们那些更具经验的职场老将中常见的经历。

sentences.en: help people through difficulties in their interpersonal relationships to our relationships with our career.
sentences.zh: 在此之后，我谈到了与工作渐行渐远。

sentences.en: Now, in the book, you outline five key drivers that make people consider leaving their jobs.
sentences.zh: 这有点像看着你的配偶，然后心里想：你究竟是谁？

sentences.en: Can you talk briefly about those?
sentences.zh: 你根本不是我娶的那个人，也不是我最初与之建立这段恋爱关系的那个人，我完全不认识你了。

sentences.en: Yes, I actually started with the toughest kind of most existential one, which is having an identity crisis at work.
sentences.zh: 当我们经历这种体验时，我们中的许多人会认为真正改变的是对方，或者用这个比喻来说，是职业变了。

sentences.en: This idea that you can just fall out of love with something that has been defining you for a really long time, that your core sense of who you are as a person, your identity as
sentences.zh: 这其实不太是我们的问题。

sentences.en: a human being is very much wrapped up in your workplace identity, but you're starting to question that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的心路历程实际上是要弄清楚到底是谁变了，你知道的，以及我自己变了多少。

sentences.en: And I think people who go through this are often very advanced in their careers.
sentences.zh: 通常我们发生改变并不是变得更好或更坏，而是以不同的方式、平行的方式在改变。

sentences.en: They've spent a lot of time and money getting there.
sentences.zh: 我也谈到了“分身乏术”这种想法。

sentences.en: They have a lot of status.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道的，书中的这一章实际上适合所有人，即使你没有遭遇职业危机。

sentences.en: And so kind of grappling with falling out of love with something that still defines you is a common experience among our kind of more well-seasoned career goers out there.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们正处于一个前所未忙的时代。

sentences.en: From there, I talk about being drifted apart from your job.
sentences.zh: 我们经常承担那些实际上并不能真正帮助我们在职业上取得进展的角色和任务，而我们自己却并不太清楚原因。

sentences.en: And this is a little bit like looking over at your spouse and thinking, who are you?
sentences.zh: 我们一直在进行任务切换。

sentences.en: You are not the person that I married, that I initially got into this romantic relationship with, I don't recognize you.
sentences.zh: 可能你的听众对这些都很熟悉：在工作通话时查看手机、检查邮件或是订购杂货。

sentences.en: And when we go through this experience, a lot of us think that it's really the other person or in this kind of metaphor, the career that's changed.
sentences.zh: 这似乎已经成了常态，而不是特例。

sentences.en: It's not so much us.
sentences.zh: （这一章旨在）帮助人们处理那些阻碍他们对工作感到满意、同时也阻碍他们前进的日常生活中的小问题。

sentences.en: And so their journey is really about understanding who's changed, you know, and how much I have changed.
sentences.zh: 然后书的最后两章不是关于你对工作失去热爱，而是关于工作没有回报你的爱。

sentences.en: And often we change, not for the better or the worse, but in different ways, in parallel ways.
sentences.zh: 我想，对于我们这些曾在职场中屈居第二的人来说，我们一直在努力争取晋升或加薪，却不知道原因何在。

sentences.en: I also talk about this kind of idea of being spread too thin.
sentences.zh: 那可能是一次非常令人沮丧的经历。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, this chapter of the book is really for everybody, even if you're not having a career crisis.
sentences.zh: 我了解到，这通常归结为巨大的沟通差距：一方面是提拔你的人告诉你——或者至少他们认为自己在暗示——你应该做些什么来获得晋升，另一方面是你认为自己应该做些什么。

sentences.en: I think we are in an age of sort of unprecedented busyness.
sentences.zh: 而这两者往往并不一致。

sentences.en: We often take on roles and tasks that really aren't actually helping us advance in our careers and we're not quite sure why.
sentences.zh: 我最后谈到的是“不被赏识的明星员工”。

sentences.en: We task switch all the time.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个为职场带来巨大贡献却只得到很多口头表扬的人。

sentences.en: Probably your listeners are familiar with checking their phones or their emails or ordering groceries while on work calls.
sentences.zh: 他们会收到很多不错的Slack频道消息和电子邮件，但却没有得到他们在乎的实质奖励。

sentences.en: This seems to be sort of the norm rather than the exception.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些人的一个挣扎，真的是要刨根问底搞清楚这个问题：我的行业到底在乎明星员工吗？

sentences.en: And helping people kind of deal with those everyday little issues that are preventing them from feeling good about their jobs, but also moving ahead.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有没有这样一个市场，能够接纳像我这样具有我的专业水平、身价如此之高的人，还是说“差不多就行”就已经足够好了？

sentences.en: And then the last two chapters of the book aren't about falling out of love with your job, but about your job not loving you back.
sentences.zh: 我在为这本书做研究时变得非常愤世嫉俗，因为答案往往就是：差不多就行了。

sentences.en: And I think for those of us who've ever been a runner up at work, we struggle with getting a promotion or raise, but we don't know why.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你没有得到你想要的东西。

sentences.en: That can be a really frustrating experience.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，这其实就是去爱一个并没有给予你回报的事物——你感觉自己正在为那份工作或职业付出，却没有得到相应的反馈。

sentences.en: And I've learned that often kind of comes down to huge communication gaps between what
sentences.zh: 我们真的应该期望爱上我们的工作吗？

sentences.en: promoters tell you, or at least they think they're implying what you should be doing to get ahead and what you think you should be doing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，工作终究是工作，而且我们在工作之外还有其他人际关系。

sentences.en: And they're often misaligned.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，这是不是对某种本质上只是给你提供金钱、让你得以生存、有个遮风挡雨的地方并有饭吃的东西赋予了太多的重要性？

sentences.en: I end up with the underappreciated star.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个问题。

sentences.en: This is the person who brings a lot to the workplace and they get a lot of pats on the back.
sentences.zh: 所以第一个答案是：绝对不是。

sentences.en: They get a lot of nice Slack channel messages and, you know, emails, but they're not rewarded in the ways they care about.
sentences.zh: 没有必要非得爱上你的工作。

sentences.en: And I think kind of one struggle for these folks is really getting down to the bottom of the question is, does my industry even care about stars?
sentences.zh: 当它成为一个问题时，是因为你身处的行业或你效力的公司期望那种级别的身份认同感，在那里所有能做得很好的人都深爱着他们的工作，并将其视为自我核心的一部分。

sentences.en: You know, is there even a market for someone with my level of expertise that costs as much as I do or is good enough just fine?
sentences.zh: 而你可能并没有与你的职业建立那种关系。

sentences.en: And I became very cynical in doing research for this book that often the answer is good enough is fine.
sentences.zh: 这种不匹配正是问题开始出错的地方。

sentences.en: And that's why you're not getting what you want.
sentences.zh: 或者你渴望爱上你的工作，但你不知道该如何做到这一点。

sentences.en: But it's really all about sort of loving something that isn't giving those things back to you that you feel like you're giving to that job or to that career.
sentences.zh: 我的确认为匹配的成分真的很关键。

sentences.en: Should we really expect to be in love with our jobs?
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，我们必须记住，我们在与职业的关系中投入的时间，要多于我们在家庭关系中投入的时间。

sentences.en: I mean, it is work after all, and we have relationships outside of work.
sentences.zh: 字面意义上的时间，我们在工作上花的小时数比在家里的还要多。

sentences.en: But, you know, is that putting too much importance on something that is basically, you know, it's giving you the money to live and work and put a roof over your head and eat food?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我做了很多关于压力传染的研究，即我们在工作中感受到的压力是如何传染给我们的家庭成员和朋友的。

sentences.en: I love this question.
sentences.zh: 这种传染的方向往往是从工作到家庭。

sentences.en: So the first answer is absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 比起从家庭到工作，这是更强的压力传染方向。

sentences.en: It is not necessary to be in love with your job.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我们花在工作上的时间，甚至比我们和孩子在一起的时间——比如抚养孩子的时间——或者和爱人在一起的时间还要多。

sentences.en: When it becomes an issue is when you are in an industry or you're working for a company that expects that level of identity commitment where everyone who thrives there is in love
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为去努力处理你有多想爱上那项事业确实很重要，但同时也不能低估你围绕它产生的负面情绪会对你真正关心的其他生活领域产生的影响。

sentences.en: with their job and they see it as a core part of who they are.
sentences.zh: 现在，你在书的引言中提到，你注意到近年来发生了一种转变，尤其是在大流行之后，人们思考和谈论他们与工作关系的方式发生了变化。

sentences.en: And you maybe don't actually have that same kind of relationship with your career.
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: That mismatch is where things start to go awry.
sentences.zh: 你认为这种转变有多少是由大流行引起的？

sentences.en: Or you want to be in love with your job, but you don't know how to get it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想，你知道的，我们首先看到这种由于对职业感到全球性的不快乐、无聊感和焦虑而带来的上升趋势是在大流行期间出现的。

sentences.en: I do think that kind of the matching component is really key.
sentences.zh: 但我感觉在大流行期间，我们更容易把矛头指向居家办公带来的压力、全球经济崩溃的压力以及人们生病的压力，并将责任归咎于它们。

sentences.en: But I also think it's important for us to remember that our relationship with our career, we spend more time in that relationship than we do in our relationships at home.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，对于那些经历职场不快的人来说，大流行是一个非常方便的替罪羊。

sentences.en: Just literal hours of the day, more of them are spent at work than they are at home.
sentences.zh: 但把时间快进几年，我们来到了这里，而人们依然感到痛苦。

sentences.en: And, you know, I do a lot of research on stress contagion, how the stress we feel at work can be caught by our family members, by our friends.
sentences.zh: 盖洛普（Gallup）刚刚发布的一项民意调查显示，19%的人对工作感到非常不快乐。

sentences.en: And the direction tends to go from work to home.
sentences.zh: 但我们却没有了同样明确的源头来归咎责任。

sentences.en: That's the stronger direction of stress contagion than home to work.
sentences.zh: 我想对于许多人来说，有一种模糊的感觉，觉得他们很痛苦，却又说不出个所以然来。

sentences.en: And it's because we spend more time at our jobs than we do even with our children, you know, even raising a child or with a loved one.
sentences.zh: 你会听到人们使用诸如因果关系的语言，比如：一旦我们公司和另一家合并了，一切就都崩溃了。

sentences.en: And so I do think it's important to really try to grapple with how much you want to be in love with that thing, but not underestimating the extent to which your negative emotions
sentences.zh: 或者：一旦我们取消了办公室、实体办公室，沟通就不再顺畅了，或者我的老板调走了。

sentences.en: around it can actually affect other types of your life that you do really care about.
sentences.zh: 所以他们一直在努力将他们的不快乐归咎于某个特定的源头。

sentences.en: Now, you mentioned in the introduction to the book that you've noticed a shift in recent years, especially post-pandemic, and how people were thinking about and talking about
sentences.zh: 但他们往往没有弄清楚，这个源头其实是他们自己对职业的心理关系，它实际上比单纯的新老板或新办公室要深刻得多。

sentences.en: their relationship with their work.
sentences.zh: 问题与其说是这些结构性的东西，不如说是这些深层的心理问题。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 这就是我所看到的自大流行以来的过去几年里发生的变化。

sentences.en: And how much of that shift do you think is due to the pandemic?
sentences.zh: 当人们对工作感到不满并开始考虑离职时——

sentences.en: Yes, I think, you know, we first saw this rise of kind of, you know, global unhappiness of ennui, of angst around our careers, rising during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你谈到了五个关键驱动因素。

sentences.en: But I felt like during the pandemic, it was much easier for us to kind of finger point and blame it on the stress we were feeling from working from home, the stress of, you
sentences.zh: 这总是一个因素，还是说它总是多个驱动因素共同作用的结果？

sentences.en: know, the global economy just crashing, people sick.
sentences.zh: 这真的是个好问题。

sentences.en: You know, the pandemic was a very easy sort of blame for people who are experiencing workplace unhappiness.
sentences.zh: 我想对我们大多数人来说，情况很复杂。

sentences.en: But you fast forward a few years, and here we are, and people are still miserable.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，我创建了一个调查来帮助你弄清楚哪个驱动因素最能引起你的共鸣，但我研究过的几乎每个人都有至少两到三个。

sentences.en: Gallup just came out with a poll showing that, you know, 19% of people are just incredibly unhappy at work.
sentences.zh: 我想几乎每个人都觉得自己在工作中心力交瘁。

sentences.en: But we don't quite have the same sort of source to blame it on.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为关键在于确定主要的驱动因素是什么，然后在此基础上，找出正在发生的次要驱动因素是什么。

sentences.en: And I think for a lot of people, there's sort of this nebulous feeling that they're miserable, and they're not quite sure why.
sentences.zh: 我认为你必须做出的唯一真正的抉择点——至少在阅读我的书时——是弄清楚你是想要一份新工作，还是想要一个全新的职业。

sentences.en: You hear people sort of use causal language, like, once our company merged with another one, everything fell apart.
sentences.zh: 那是你需要努力解决的重大心理问题之一。

sentences.en: Or once we got rid of, you know, our in-office, our brick-and-mortar office, communication was no longer good, or my boss moved.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，就这些心理驱动因素而言，我们大多数人的情况都相当复杂。

sentences.en: So they're grappling with trying to sort of blame their unhappiness on a particular source.
sentences.zh: 让我们暂时转换一下话题，谈谈你的第一本书《职场混蛋》（Jerks at Work），这是一个很棒的书名。

sentences.en: But they're not often sort of figuring out that that source is really their own kind of psychological relationship with their career, that it's actually kind of much deeper than
sentences.zh: 你在书中指出了职场中的五种不同类型的混蛋。

sentences.en: just a new boss or a new office.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，你能简要描述一下他们以及他们的性格特征吗？

sentences.en: It isn't so much these structural things, but these kind of deep psychological issues.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: And that's kind of the shift that I've seen in the last couple years since the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 所以第一种是“向上谄媚、向下踩踏的人”（kiss-up kick-downer）。

sentences.en: When people are feeling dissatisfied with their jobs, and they start to think about leaving,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果有人曾在这样一个地方工作过：他们有一个同事，你知道的，非常虐待与他们同级别或职位比他们低的人，但老板却很爱这个同事。

sentences.en: I mean, you talked about five key drivers.
sentences.zh: 他们是高绩效员工。

sentences.en: Is it always, is it just one, or is it always just a multiplicity of drivers?
sentences.zh: 你一定懂那种令人不安的感觉：由于某个被高层地位的人宠爱的人挡了你的路，你无法获得晋升。

sentences.en: That's a really good question.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我认为“向上谄媚、向下踩踏的人”是一种很常见的经历，特别是在我们许多人曾经经历过的相当残酷的职业生涯中。

sentences.en: I think for most of us, there's a lot going on.
sentences.zh: 我曾在鞋业工作过。

sentences.en: I think, you know, I created a survey to help you figure out what driver most strongly resonates with you, but almost everyone who I studied has at least two or three.
sentences.zh: 我曾在销售行业工作过。

sentences.en: I think almost everyone feels, you know, spread too thin at work.
sentences.zh: 而我就是在学术界发现了这种人。

sentences.en: So I think the key is identifying sort of what is the main driver, and then from there, what are the kind of secondary order drivers that are going on?
sentences.zh: 这里有很多“向上谄媚、向下踩踏的人”。

sentences.en: The only real choice point I think you have to make, at least in reading my book, is figuring out if you want a new job or a completely new career.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们还要面对其他类型很难相处的人。

sentences.en: That's kind of one of those big psychological questions that you need to grapple with.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，职场上有“推土机型”的人，他们不仅在会议上喋喋不休，而且实际上还会在幕后利用他们的地位和权力来破坏群体的流程。

sentences.en: But most of us have a lot going on in terms of those psychological drivers, for sure.
sentences.zh: 我们在招聘委员会等事情上经常看到这种情况，他们的讨论总是陷入僵局，却又说不出原因。

sentences.en: Let's shift gears for a minute and talk about your first book, Jerks at Work, which is a great title.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，是一个“推土机”在跟老板或老板的老板谈话，说：“我这里不喜欢这个流程，”因为他们中意的人选没有被选中。

sentences.en: You identified five different types of jerks at work.
sentences.zh: 这些是他们耍出的聪明的、诡计多端的把戏。

sentences.en: Can you briefly, if that's possible, describe them and what their character traits are?
sentences.zh: 我们在职场中还会遇到“窃取功劳者”，这些人可能会为了表现得像个团队合作者而为你的一些小事记功，但实际上他们却把更大的功劳据为己有。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们很难弄清楚自己到底应得多少功劳。

sentences.en: So the first is the kiss-up kick-downer.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人认为自己应得大部分功劳。

sentences.en: So if anyone's ever worked in a place where they have a colleague who, you know, really mistreats people at the same level as them or beneath them, but the boss loves this person.
sentences.zh: 因此，分配功劳、弄清楚这个过程是围绕这类型人的主要问题之一。

sentences.en: They're a high performer.
sentences.zh: 然后我还谈到了“搭便车”（free riding），这是无处不在的。

sentences.en: You know this sort of unnerving feeling of not being able to get ahead because someone's blocking you who is just adored by people high status.
sentences.zh: 每个人都遇到过有搭便车者的团队。

sentences.en: And, you know, the kiss-up kick-downer I think is a common experience, especially in pretty kind of cut-throat careers that a lot of us, you know, have been in.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: I worked in shoes.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: I worked in sales.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: And this is where I identified this person in academia.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: There's plenty of kiss-up kick-downers.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: But I think there's other types of people that we deal with that are difficult.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: You know, there's bulldozers at work, the people who don't just kind of talk the whole time in a meeting, but actually go behind the scenes to leverage their status and power
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: to disrupt group processes.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: And we see this a lot with things like hiring committees where they just keep ending in an impasse and they're not quite sure why.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: And it turns out a bulldozer is talking to the boss or the boss's boss and saying, I don't like the process here because their candidate wasn't chosen.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: These kind of clever tricksy moves that they do.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: We also have credit stealers at work, people who will maybe give you credit for small things
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: in an attempt to look like a team player, but they actually are taking credit for the bigger things.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: And I think it's very difficult for us to kind of know how much credit we deserve.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: Most of us think we deserve most of it.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: So allocating credit, figuring out that process is kind of one of the main issues around that one.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: And then I also talk about free writing, which is just ubiquitous.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: Everyone's been on a team with free writers.
sentences.zh: 在这里插入补充

sentences.en: One thing a lot of us don't realize is free writers tend to be well-liked, well-connected people who bring something to the team.
sentences.zh: 许多人没有意识到的一点是，自由写手往往是受欢迎、人脉广且能为团队带来价值的人。

sentences.en: Often it's gossip or fun or the ability to get dinner reservations, something that acts as a social glue in the group.
sentences.zh: 通常是八卦、乐趣或预订晚餐的能力，这种东西就像群体中的社交黏合剂。

sentences.en: And for that reason, they're able to kind of allocate all their work freely among all the other members and get away with it.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，他们能够将所有工作自由分配给其他所有成员，却还能安然脱身。

sentences.en: I also talk about a couple of different types of bosses.
sentences.zh: 我还谈到了几种不同类型的老板。

sentences.en: The micromanager, who most of us are probably also familiar with, that person who works all the time but gets nothing done.
sentences.zh: 微观管理者，我们大多数人可能也很熟悉，那种整天工作却什么也干不成的人。

sentences.en: I actually feel for these people.
sentences.zh: 我其实挺同情这些人的。

sentences.en: They often just receive poor training.
sentences.zh: 他们通常只是受过糟糕的培训。

sentences.en: And then the other side of that is this neglectful boss.
sentences.zh: 而另一面则是这种甩手掌柜似的老板。

sentences.en: And often we actually see the two kind of going hand in hand.
sentences.zh: 而且我们经常看到这两种情况齐头并进。

sentences.en: While I'm micromanaging you, I'm neglecting someone else.
sentences.zh: 当我对你进行微观管理时，我就在忽视其他人。

sentences.en: And that neglectful boss kind of goes in and out of caring.
sentences.zh: 而那种甩手掌柜老板对关心与否总是忽冷忽热。

sentences.en: They show up at the 11th hour.
sentences.zh: 他们在最后关头才出现。

sentences.en: They put their foot down.
sentences.zh: 他们态度强硬。

sentences.en: They demand changes.
sentences.zh: 他们要求改变。

sentences.en: And then they disappear again.
sentences.zh: 然后又消失了。

sentences.en: And it's just a very sort of anxiety-provoking experience.
sentences.zh: 这实在是一种非常催生焦虑的体验。

sentences.en: And then I end with a gaslighter.
sentences.zh: 最后我以煤气灯操纵者结尾。

sentences.en: And this is, you know, probably the most pathological of all the people I talk about.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这可以说是我所谈论的人当中病态最严重的一种。

sentences.en: These individuals lie with the intent of deceiving on a very big scale, often to cover something up
sentences.zh: 这些家伙大规模地怀着欺骗的目的撒谎，通常是为了掩盖什么

sentences.en: or to get you to be involved in something that they don't want others knowing about.
sentences.zh: 或者让你卷入一些他们不想让别人知道的事情中。

sentences.en: And the psychological damage that they do can last, you know, 10, 20, 30 years.
sentences.zh: 他们造成的心理伤害可以持续，你知道，10年、20年、30年。

sentences.en: And the victims of gaslighters often feel socially isolated.
sentences.zh: 煤气灯操纵者的受害者往往会感到社交孤立。

sentences.en: And they feel like they don't know who they can go to for help.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得不知道该找谁寻求帮助。

sentences.en: Out of all the types of jurors I talk about, I think most of them are kind of accidental or unaware to some degree, with the exception of the first and the last, that gaslighter
sentences.zh: 在我谈到的所有类型的同事中，我认为大多数人在某种程度上都是无意的或不知情的，除了第一种和最后一种，也就是那个煤气灯操纵者

sentences.en: and that kiss-up kick-downer.
sentences.zh: 还有那个媚上欺下的人。

sentences.en: They tend to actually be acting out in kind of self-interested ways.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上往往出于自私的动机行事。

sentences.en: Others, maybe not so much.
sentences.zh: 其他人可能就没那么严重了。

sentences.en: Which raises the question, and I know you get asked this all the time, but how do you know that you're not the jerk at work?
sentences.zh: 这就引出了一个问题，我知道人们经常问你这个，但你如何知道自己不是工作中的讨厌鬼？

sentences.en: Well, don't expect anyone to tell you if you are the jerk at work.
sentences.zh: 嗯，别指望会有人告诉你你是不是工作中的讨厌鬼。

sentences.en: One of the things I study a lot is feedback and how terrible we are at it and how anxious it makes us to be forthcoming.
sentences.zh: 我经常研究的事情之一就是反馈，以及我们在这方面有多糟糕，坦率地表达会让我们多么焦虑。

sentences.en: And so I think for a lot of jerks, they have to learn to read the tea leaves in interesting ways.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为对于许多讨厌鬼来说，他们必须学会以有趣的方式察言观色。

sentences.en: I think kind of one of the kind of more interesting ways that they learn about this is when they apply for new jobs.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们了解这一点的一个更有趣的方式是当他们申请新工作时。

sentences.en: And when that job seeks out recommendations or references, they get crickets in return.
sentences.zh: 当那份工作寻找推荐信或证明人时，他们却得到了死一般的寂静。

sentences.en: It's not that anyone says anything bad, they just don't say anything good.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说有人说坏话，只是他们什么好话也不说。

sentences.en: And at NYU, I handle a lot of promotions among our professors, and we can tell if someone's a jerk when we solicit 20 letters and get two back, for instance.
sentences.zh: 在纽约大学，我处理很多教授的晋升事宜，如果我们发出20封信却只收到2封回复，我们就能看出某人是不是个讨厌鬼。

sentences.en: Those are the kinds of clues.
sentences.zh: 这就是这类线索。

sentences.en: And so if you're worried about being a jerk, there is kind of a formula you need to follow
sentences.zh: 所以如果你担心自己是个讨厌鬼，你需要遵循某种公式

sentences.en: of how to ask for very specific feedback following anything you've done that isn't about your reputation, but more about your specific behaviors.
sentences.zh: 即在你做了任何事情之后，如何要求非常具体的反馈，这无关你的声誉，而是更多关于你的具体行为。

sentences.en: But I do think that a lot of us walk around, and I do a lot of one-on-one coaching, and I
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为我们很多人四处走动，我做了很多一对一的辅导，我

sentences.en: find that people who are being coached because their boss thinks they're a jerk are just heartbroken when they find out that that's why they're in this meeting with me.
sentences.zh: 发现那些因为老板认为他们是讨厌鬼而接受辅导的人，当他们发现这就是他们来参加我和这个会议的原因时，心碎不已。

sentences.en: You know, oh, I'm so excited for this leadership training.
sentences.zh: 你知道，哦，我对这次领导力培训太兴奋了。

sentences.en: And I'm like, this is not leadership training.
sentences.zh: 而我会说，这不是领导力培训。

sentences.en: I'm supposed to de-jerk you.
sentences.zh: 我是来帮你戒掉讨厌鬼习气的。

sentences.en: And your boss didn't want to tell you, so here I am, welcome, to deliver the news for you.
sentences.zh: 你的老板不想告诉你，所以我就在这里，欢迎，来为你传递这个消息。

sentences.en: And then they cry and get over it, and then we move on from there.
sentences.zh: 然后他们哭过之后就接受了，接着我们从那里继续前进。

sentences.en: But it's often a pretty heart-wrenching experience.
sentences.zh: 但这通常是一次相当揪心的经历。

sentences.en: And can jerks be rehabilitated?
sentences.zh: 讨厌鬼能改过自新吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 能。

sentences.en: I think that not every jerk can be rehabilitated.
sentences.zh: 我认为并不是每个讨厌鬼都能改过自新。

sentences.en: But by and large, jerks tend to grow out of systems and structures that are, you know, in place to help sort of thrive in those situations.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，讨厌鬼往往是在那些，你知道的，为了帮助在这些情况下蓬勃发展而建立的系统和结构中滋生出来的。

sentences.en: You know, there are kind of hierarchies at work that are zero-sum, where kiss-up, kick-downers can only get ahead by doing that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，工作中存在某种零和博弈的等级制度，媚上欺下者只有通过这种方式才能出人头地。

sentences.en: They're Machiavellian.
sentences.zh: 他们是马基雅维利式的。

sentences.en: Everyone who's made it before them was also Machiavellian.
sentences.zh: 他们之前的所有成功者也都是马基雅维利式的。

sentences.en: And what do you expect when you are reinforcing that kind of thing?
sentences.zh: 当你助长这种事情时，你还能期望什么呢？

sentences.en: And so I think when bosses and people like that try to play whack-a-mole with their jerks,
sentences.zh: 所以我想，当老板和这样的人试图对他们的讨厌鬼玩打地鼠游戏时，

sentences.en: I usually tell them to stop, look at the systems and structures you have in place, and look
sentences.zh: 我通常告诉他们停下来，看看你们现有的系统和结构，看看

sentences.en: at your interview questions, and look at your onboarding, and are you doing things to allow jerks to thrive here?
sentences.zh: 你们的面试问题，看看你们的入职培训，你们做的事情是不是在允许讨厌鬼在这里滋生？

sentences.en: What is the culture?
sentences.zh: 什么是文化？

sentences.en: And I know that's a big nebulous word, but it comes down to, like, what are your processes and procedures that are inadvertently creating a fertile breeding ground for jerks?
sentences.zh: 我知道这是一个庞大而模糊的词，但归根结底，比如，你们的哪些流程和程序在无意中为讨厌鬼创造了肥沃的滋生土壤？

sentences.en: So to that end, I think, yes, most can be by changing structures and systeMs.
sentences.zh: 为此，我认为，是的，通过改变结构和系统，大多数人是可以改变的。

sentences.en: So for our listeners who might be interviewing for a new job, what can they do to make sure that they're not walking into a workplace that's populated by jerks?
sentences.zh: 所以对于那些可能正在面试新工作的听众，他们可以做些什么来确保自己不会走进一个到处都是讨厌鬼的工作场所？

sentences.en: Or to take it beyond the negative, walking into a workplace where they think they might fall in love?
sentences.zh: 或者抛开消极的一面不谈，走进一个他们认为自己可能会坠入爱河的工作场所？

sentences.en: This is a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: I think that the single thing that you can do that you have control over is to speak to as many people as you can who work in that organization, not necessarily in your role or
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以做的、并且由你掌控的唯一事情，就是尽可能多地与在该组织工作过的人交谈，不一定非要在你的岗位上或

sentences.en: on your team, but in kind of parallel parts of the organization, past and present.
sentences.zh: 你的团队里，而是在组织中平行部门的过去和现在的员工。

sentences.en: You know, in job therapy, I talk a lot about networking, which feels like a yucky word for people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在职业治疗中，我经常谈论人脉拓展，对人们来说这似乎是个令人讨厌的词。

sentences.en: But networking really comes down to information gathering.
sentences.zh: 但拓展人脉其实归根结底就是收集信息。

sentences.en: It means learning new things.
sentences.zh: 这意味着了解新事物。

sentences.en: It means learning hidden curriculum and norms around a workplace that normally you wouldn't experience until you're already working there.
sentences.zh: 这意味着了解工作场所周围隐藏的课程和规范，通常在你真正开始工作之前你是体验不到的。

sentences.en: Most of us only interface with hiring managers.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人只与招聘经理对接。

sentences.en: We don't actually ask hiring managers, can I talk to team members, you know, who work in this organization?
sentences.zh: 我们其实并没有问招聘经理，我能和在这个组织工作的团队成员聊聊吗？

sentences.en: And if you don't know what to say to them because you're afraid they're not going to say anything bad about the organization, just you can ask one simple question, which is,
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道该对他们说什么，因为你害怕他们不会说关于这个组织的任何坏话，你只需问一个简单的问题，那就是：

sentences.en: finish the sentence.
sentences.zh: 补全这句话。

sentences.en: Before I started this job, nobody told me that.
sentences.zh: 在我开始这份工作之前，没有人告诉我...

sentences.en: And you will get all kinds of fascinating answers around hidden norms, around expectations, around roles.
sentences.zh: 你会得到关于隐藏规范、期望、角色的各种迷人答案。

sentences.en: I surveyed lots of people and asked them this question.
sentences.zh: 我调查了很多人并问了他们这个问题。

sentences.en: And most of the answers came down to things that they were expected to do as part of the role that were not advertised ever, not in the job advertisement, not were discussed,
sentences.zh: 大多数答案都归结为他们被期望作为角色一部分去做的事情，而这些事情从来没有被宣传过，无论是招聘广告中还是讨论中都没有，

sentences.en: and norms around interpersonal dynamics at work.
sentences.zh: 还有关于工作中人际交往动态的规范。

sentences.en: Things that they were expected to do to get ahead, people they were expected to talk to, ways that they were expected to respect one another.
sentences.zh: 为了出人头地而被期望做的事情，被期望交谈的人，被期望如何相互尊重的方式。

sentences.en: All of these kinds of messy, fun, interpersonal dynamics.
sentences.zh: 所有这些乱七八糟、有趣的人际交往动态。

sentences.en: And that one question will shed a whole bunch of light on what an organization is actually like to work for.
sentences.zh: 而这一个问题将为一家组织实际的工作体验带来大量光亮。

sentences.en: When you're doing that kind of homework, I just want to ask about some of these websites, places like Glassdoor, for example.
sentences.zh: 当你做这种功课时，我只想问问其中一些网站，比如像Glassdoor这样的地方。

sentences.en: Do you think it's worth going there?
sentences.zh: 你觉得去那里值得吗？

sentences.en: Or is that just a place for people who are really upset and disgruntled to let it all out?
sentences.zh: 还是那只是一群非常沮丧和不满的人发泄情绪的地方？

sentences.en: Glassdoor is a lot like teaching evaluations for professors.
sentences.zh: Glassdoor很像教授的教学评估。

sentences.en: You will get two answers.
sentences.zh: 你会得到两种答案。

sentences.en: I love it here.
sentences.zh: 我爱这里。

sentences.en: It's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 这里太棒了。

sentences.en: I hate it here.
sentences.zh: 我恨这里。

sentences.en: It's terrible.
sentences.zh: 这里太糟糕了。

sentences.en: People who are in the middle of the distribution of happiness who are, it's fine.
sentences.zh: 那些处于幸福分布中间的人，觉得还行。

sentences.en: It's not great.
sentences.zh: 不算太好。

sentences.en: They tend to not put ratings on Glassdoor.
sentences.zh: 他们往往不会在Glassdoor上给出评分。

sentences.en: And this is true for all kinds of ratings from Airbnb to Amazon to, you know, as a professor, the teaching evaluations I get.
sentences.zh: 从Airbnb到亚马逊的各种评分都是如此，你知道，作为一名教授，我得到的教学评估也是如此。

sentences.en: And so just know that if you're reading those things on Glassdoor, you're getting a pretty biased sample.
sentences.zh: 所以要知道，如果你在Glassdoor上阅读这些内容，你得到的样本是相当有偏见的。

sentences.en: You're getting the lovers and the haters.
sentences.zh: 你得到的是热爱者和痛恨者。

sentences.en: What you don't know is how representative those lovers and haters are of the general group of people who work there.
sentences.zh: 你所不知道的是，这些热爱者和痛恨者在多大程度上代表了在那里工作的人的总群体。

sentences.en: You know, if there's five negative reviews, does that mean that 50% of the people who are miserable and you're getting that good selection?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果有五条负面评论，这是否意味着50%的人都很痛苦，而你得到了这种良好的选择性？

sentences.en: Or does that mean 1% are miserable?
sentences.zh: 还是说这意味着1%的人感到痛苦？

sentences.en: You also don't know whether those people are all networked with each other.
sentences.zh: 你也不知道这些人彼此之间是否都有人脉关系。

sentences.en: And what you're actually getting is one experience through five voices or five unique experiences that are all representative of a different problem.
sentences.zh: 而你实际得到的是通过五个声音表达的一种体验，或者是代表不同问题的五个独特体验。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, any time you network with people at work, you're able to kind of suss out how much of this is due to, say, a common boss or, you know, a past office that
sentences.zh: 我想你知道，任何时候你在工作中与人建立人脉，你都能够查明其中有多少是由于，比方说，一个共同的老板，或者，你知道，一个有着

sentences.en: had a bad culture versus kind of individual experiences.
sentences.zh: 糟糕文化的过去办公室，还是个人经历造成的。

sentences.en: And so that's what one-on-one conversations will give you above and beyond Glassdoor.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是一对一对话能带给你、且远超Glassdoor的地方。

sentences.en: I know people love reading ratings and reading a lot into them.
sentences.zh: 我知道人们喜欢阅读评分并对它们进行深入解读。

sentences.en: It's a passive experience.
sentences.zh: 这是一种被动的体验。

sentences.en: It's an anxiety-free experience.
sentences.zh: 这是一种无焦虑的体验。

sentences.en: Talking to people is harder.
sentences.zh: 与人交谈更难。

sentences.en: It's more uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 更不舒服。

sentences.en: It's more awkward.
sentences.zh: 更尴尬。

sentences.en: But it's just less rich data that you're getting when you do that.
sentences.zh: 但当你这样做时，获得的数据却远没有那么丰富。

sentences.en: Spoken like a scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 说得真像个科学家。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, APA recently published our annual Work in America survey, which looks at how people are feeling about their workplaces and their work lives.
sentences.zh: 现在，美国心理协会最近发布了我们的年度“美国工作”调查，该调查着眼于人们对工作场所和工作生活的感受。

sentences.en: And one of the major themes that came out this year was around psychological safety at
sentences.zh: 今年出现的一个主要主题围绕着工作场所的

sentences.en: work, the idea that people who feel psychologically safe are more satisfied and happier in their careers.
sentences.zh: 心理安全，即感到心理安全的人在职业生涯中更满意、更快乐的观点。

sentences.en: I'm curious about how you react to that.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道你对此有何反应。

sentences.en: Can a culture of psychological safety deter jerkiness and really make it more of a workplace where you will be happy and fall in love?
sentences.zh: 心理安全文化能阻止混蛋行为，并真正使其成为一个你会感到快乐并坠入爱河的工作场所吗？

sentences.en: I keep using that metaphor.
sentences.zh: 我一直在用那个隐喻。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: You're trapped now with falling in love with your career.
sentences.zh: 你现在被对职业生涯坠入爱河所困住了。

sentences.en: I forced it on you and now you're never going to be able to think about a job another way is like a romantic partner that I did not choose.
sentences.zh: 我把它强加给你，现在你永远无法以另一种方式看待工作，就像我没有选择的浪漫伴侣一样。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think psychological safety is a really interesting concept and it's one that a lot of us, especially Gen Z and millennials, love.
sentences.zh: 我认为心理安全是一个非常有趣的概念，我们很多人，尤其是Z世代和千禧一代，都非常喜欢它。

sentences.en: I do think that when we think we need to be a little critical about what it takes to be psychologically safe because I think there's a lot of work showing that people value
sentences.zh: 我确实认为，当我们思考时，我们需要对实现心理安全所需要的东西持一点批判态度，因为我认为有很多研究表明人们重视

sentences.en: psychological safety.
sentences.zh: 心理安全。

sentences.en: But what they find that threatens it is often things like clear, critical feedback, you know,
sentences.zh: 但他们发现威胁到这一点的往往是诸如清晰、批判性的反馈之类的事情，你知道的，

sentences.en: because they haven't quite developed the muscle for it or because their organization hasn't shown
sentences.zh: 因为他们还没有完全培养出应对这种反馈的能力，或者因为他们的组织没有向

sentences.en: them the right way of delivering and receiving that feedback in a psychologically safe way.
sentences.zh: 他们展示以心理安全的方式提供和接受这种反馈的正确方法。

sentences.en: So I think the concept is super important and you want to feel like if you get negative feedback
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这个概念超级重要，你希望觉得如果从老板那里得到负面反馈，

sentences.en: from your boss or you give it even upward to a boss that you're not going to face negative repercussions socially for it.
sentences.zh: 或者甚至向上给老板反馈，你不会因此在社交上面临负面影响。

sentences.en: It takes a lot of work for an organization to be able to do both things at once, give you that critical
sentences.zh: 一个组织需要付出很大努力才能同时做好两件事：给你批判性

sentences.en: feedback, give you what you need to succeed, help you network and also make you feel safe at the same time.
sentences.zh: 反馈，给你成功所需的东西，帮助你建立人脉，同时也让你感到安全。

sentences.en: And I'm saying this having read, you know, APA's kind of stress report, which shows that Gen Z
sentences.zh: 我说这话是在阅读了，你知道的，美国心理协会的压力报告之后，该报告显示Z世代

sentences.en: and millennials are through the roof and how anxious they're feeling, how stressed they're feeling,
sentences.zh: 和千禧一代的焦虑感和压力感达到了极点，

sentences.en: and then the likelihood that they're going to quit a job because of those things.
sentences.zh: 以及他们因为这些原因而辞职的可能性。

sentences.en: And so I do think we kind of need to square that circle a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为我们需要稍微圆满地解决这个难题。

sentences.en: We need to figure out how we can create psychological safety while people are stressed and anxious at work and while they also
sentences.zh: 我们需要弄清楚如何在人们在工作中感到压力和焦虑的同时创造心理安全，而他们同时

sentences.en: need that negative feedback to kind of move forward or not negative, but critical feedback, specific feedback to actually move forward.
sentences.zh: 又需要这种负面反馈来前进，或者说不是负面，而是批判性反馈、具体反馈来真正向前迈进。

sentences.en: And it's a lot of kind of complex concepts kind of all being, you know, working at one time that I think we do need to do some work to figure out how to make
sentences.zh: 这有很多复杂的概念同时在起作用，我认为我们确实需要做一些工作来弄清楚如何让

sentences.en: them all kind of work in unison.
sentences.zh: 它们协同工作。

sentences.en: Another conclusion that we reached looking at the data from that
sentences.zh: 我们从该调查的数据中得出的另一个结论是

sentences.en: survey was that there are issues, intergenerational issues in the workplace that are happening right now.
sentences.zh: 目前工作场所中存在问题，代际问题正在发生。

sentences.en: And we're probably for the first time ever, you know, in a situation where there can be as many as five generations in a single workplace.
sentences.zh: 我们可能是有史以来第一次，你知道的，处在一个单一工作场所中有多达五代人的情况。

sentences.en: We're finding that the younger folks are not relating well to the people who are older.
sentences.zh: 我们发现年轻人与年长者相处得并不好。

sentences.en: Are you seeing things like this as well in your work?
sentences.zh: 你在工作中也看到了这样的事情吗？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, we could take this conversation in so many directions.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，我们可以将这次对话引向如此多的方向。

sentences.en: I think we're seeing it with retirements among boomers, a lack of urgency to retire.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在婴儿潮一代的退休潮中看到了这一点，他们缺乏退休的紧迫感。

sentences.en: I think the ways in which older generations prefer to communicate with one another are very different than the ways in which younger generations prefer to communicate.
sentences.zh: 我认为老一辈人首选的沟通方式与年轻一代首选的沟通方式有很大不同。

sentences.en: Older generations prefer face-to-face communications, phone calls if that can't work out.
sentences.zh: 老一辈人更喜欢面对面沟通，如果行不通的话，其次是打电话。

sentences.en: They don't like, you know, Zoom calls, Slack channels, those kind of communication channels that give you less information.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们不喜欢Zoom会议、Slack频道那些信息量较少的沟通渠道。

sentences.en: They prefer more frequent interactions, not formal interactions.
sentences.zh: 他们更喜欢更频繁的互动，而不是形式化的互动。

sentences.en: And above all else, they prefer you to confront them face-to-face, not to do it on TikTok, not to do it publicly.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，他们希望你当面找他们对质，而不是在TikTok上，也不是在公开场合。

sentences.en: And I think there are norm differences around confrontation, around comfort around these things, a lot of which are rising from these anxiety differences that we're seeing in
sentences.zh: 我认为，在对质以及对这些事情的舒适度方面，存在着规范上的差异，其中很多源于我们在

sentences.en: generations and mental health issues.
sentences.zh: 各代人和心理健康问题中看到的焦虑差异。

sentences.en: And I think the older generations are less comfortable with things like generative AI being used at work.
sentences.zh: 我认为老一辈对在工作中使用生成式AI这类事情没那么适应。

sentences.en: They want a more sort of organic human, you know, past the Turing test kind of experience.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一种更自然的人际交流，你知道的，那种能通过图灵测试的体验。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, one thing that we're not doing a lot in this conversation is talking about what older generations have that is better than younger generations.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，在这个对话中，我们有一件事做得不够，那就是讨论老一辈拥有而年轻一代没有的优势。

sentences.en: They are less anxious.
sentences.zh: 他们的焦虑感更少。

sentences.en: They have richer social networks.
sentences.zh: 他们的社交网络更丰富。

sentences.en: They have tacit knowledge and experience with mentorship that we often kind of throw aside and say, why can't you just leave?
sentences.zh: 他们拥有隐性知识和指导经验，而我们常常把这些抛在一边，说，你们怎么还不走？

sentences.en: Why can't you just retire and make room for the younger people?
sentences.zh: 为什么不直接退休，给年轻人腾出位置呢？

sentences.en: And I think that we are, it's a huge missed opportunity there.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个巨大的错失良机。

sentences.en: In defense of the boomers, I really do think, you know, it's a missed, and Gen Xers, it's a missed opportunity to actually enrich in communication.
sentences.zh: 为婴儿潮一代辩护的话，我真的认为，对于X世代来说，这也是一个丰富沟通的错失良机。

sentences.en: And I say this knowing that AI is taking over a lot of jobs, but what it's not
sentences.zh: 我说这话时知道人工智能正在接管许多工作，但它没有

sentences.en: taking over the human interfacing ones, things like hospitality, healthcare, things that require you to communicate well with another person.
sentences.zh: 接管的是需要人际接口的工作，比如酒店业、医疗保健业、需要你与另一个人良好沟通的事情。

sentences.en: And older generations tend to actually be much better at that than younger generations.
sentences.zh: 而且老一辈人往往在这方面比年轻一代做得好得多。

sentences.en: So, you know, I'm all about like, let's bring that knowledge in to kind of help solve some of these intergenerational issues that we're seeing at work.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我全力支持将这种知识引入进来，以帮助解决我们在工作中看到的一些代际问题。

sentences.en: So I want to switch topics to exit interviews.
sentences.zh: 我想把话题转到离职面谈上。

sentences.en: I read an article in which you said that the default response in exit interviews is to lie, is bull.
sentences.zh: 我读过一篇文章，你在里面说离职面谈中的默认回应是说谎，这简直是胡扯。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering then, is there any value to exit interviews?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，离职面谈还有价值吗？

sentences.en: And if you're the exit interviewee, what's the best way to handle an exit interview and make it worth everyone's time?
sentences.zh: 如果你是接受离职面谈的人，处理离职面谈并让它物有所值的最好方式是什么？

sentences.en: Yes, I think that I'm pretty sure you're referencing this Wall Street Journal article I wrote about it, all the lies we tell at work, all the ways in which we lie.
sentences.zh: 是的，我很确定你指的是我写的那篇关于《华尔街日报》的文章，关于我们在工作中说过的所有谎言，我们说谎的种种方式。

sentences.en: Exit interviews, when they're often framed from, you know, a hires or organizational perspective, it's, it's a, it's HR person asking you why you're leaving, often in these
sentences.zh: 离职面谈，当它们通常从雇主或组织的视角来构建时，是HR人员询问你为什么要离职，

sentences.en: kind of broad ways that don't get at specific issues you've might've faced.
sentences.zh: 通常是通过这种宽泛的方式，而没有触及你可能面临的具体问题。

sentences.en: And if you are to be completely honest, there could be a major sort of loss to your reputation and status.
sentences.zh: 如果你完全诚实，你的声誉和地位可能会受到重大损失。

sentences.en: And so what organizations aren't thinking about is what would this person have to gain by being honest?
sentences.zh: 因此，组织没有考虑到的是，这个人通过诚实能得到什么好处？

sentences.en: Why would they want to tell the truth?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要说实话？

sentences.en: And you know, what, if, if you're never going to talk to these people again, why would you sort of give them that kind of feedback?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果，如果你再也不会和这些人说话了，你为什么要向他们提供这种反馈呢？

sentences.en: So I think if you want honest answers, you can't wait first till the exit interview to actually ask those questions.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，如果你想要诚实的答案，你不能等到离职面谈时才去问这些问题。

sentences.en: You know, and if you're the employee, you need to insist that these questions are asked at multiple stages
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你是员工，你需要坚持在你在职期间的

sentences.en: during your time there.
sentences.zh: 多个阶段都提出这些问题。

sentences.en: I actually don't think it's up to the employee to be honest in these interviews unless they're given an incentive to do so.
sentences.zh: 其实我认为不应该由员工在这些面谈中保持诚实，除非他们被给予这样做的动力。

sentences.en: Many of them are going to rely on these places to give them recommendations for the future and it's harming their reputations to be honeSt. So if you want
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人要依靠这些地方来提供未来的推荐信，说实话会损害他们的声誉。所以如果你想要

sentences.en: honest answers, ask very specific questions that would be difficult to lie about.
sentences.zh: 诚实的答案，就要问那些很难说谎的具体问题。

sentences.en: If you want, you know, friendly overtures, ask, how was your time here?
sentences.zh: 如果你想要客套的寒暄，就问，你在这里过得怎么样？

sentences.en: How was your boss?
sentences.zh: 你的老板怎么样？

sentences.en: You know, things that are so vague, they could really mean anything.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些非常模糊、几乎可以指任何事情的问题。

sentences.en: And you're just going to get a lot of head nods and smiles and say, I just had a better opportunity elsewhere without the truth because you haven't
sentences.zh: 然后你只会得到大量的点头和微笑，并听到“我在别处有更好的发展机会”这样的话，却听不到实话，因为你在他们

sentences.en: been asking for the truth the entire time that they were here.
sentences.zh: 在这里的整个过程中根本没有要求过实话。

sentences.en: As the famous saying goes, you can't handle the truth.
sentences.zh: 正如那句名言所说，你承受不起真相。

sentences.en: Yeah, they also don't.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们也没有。

sentences.en: I'll add one other thing.
sentences.zh: 我还要补充一点。

sentences.en: A lot of organizations don't have a plan of what they actually do with exit interview data.
sentences.zh: 许多组织根本没有计划好如何处理离职面谈的数据。

sentences.en: They sort of collect it.
sentences.zh: 他们只是收集它们。

sentences.en: You don't know what they're going to do with that.
sentences.zh: 你根本不知道他们会对这些数据做什么。

sentences.en: Are they going to give it to your boss?
sentences.zh: 他们会把它交给你老板吗？

sentences.en: Are they going to just stick it in a file and never look at it again?
sentences.zh: 他们会把它塞进文件夹里再也不看一眼吗？

sentences.en: You need to be transparent about what you're actually using these data for and, you know, tell people that so that they have some sense of what their information is being used for.
sentences.zh: 你们需要对这些数据的实际用途保持透明，你知道的，告诉大家，好让大家知道自己的信息被用在了哪里。

sentences.en: Now, your academic research is about interpersonal communication and miscommunication in many different settings and situations, not just at work.
sentences.zh: 现在，你的学术研究主要关于人际交往以及在各种不同环境和情境下的沟通误解，不仅仅是在工作中。

sentences.en: But why is it important for people to think about the potential for miscommunication on the job?
sentences.zh: 但为什么人们认为思考工作中的沟通误解潜力是很重要的呢？

sentences.en: So I think most of us are worse communicators than we realize, partly because we have a major
sentences.zh: 我认为我们大多数人的沟通能力比自己意识到的还要糟糕，部分原因是我们有一种重大的

sentences.en: kind of transparency bias that we think our thoughts and feelings are just going to be sort of readable to other people.
sentences.zh: 透明度偏见，认为我们的想法和感受很容易被其他人理解。

sentences.en: There's a lot of reasons why that's not true.
sentences.zh: 有很多原因说明事实并非如此。

sentences.en: In fact, I spent 20 years trying to get people to be more accurate at reading one another in interpersonal interactions and in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我花了20年时间试图让人在人际交往和职场中更准确地解读彼此。

sentences.en: And the only magic bullet is to ask, what are you thinking?
sentences.zh: 而唯一的万灵药就是去问：你在想什么？

sentences.en: What did you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: And I think a lot of us walk around at work kind of underestimating the value of clear,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们很多人在工作中四处走动时，都低估了清晰、

sentences.en: consistent communication in developing better skills at work, at learning how to perform at work.
sentences.zh: 连贯的沟通在培养更好工作技能、学习如何在职场中表现方面的价值。

sentences.en: So everything from making small corrections early on in your career, like a Matthew effect that will
sentences.zh: 所以，从职业生涯早期做出小调整——就像马太效应一样，

sentences.en: then help you grow later, to understanding why you didn't get a raise or promotion.
sentences.zh: 会帮助你日后成长——到理解为什么你没有得到加薪或晋升，所有这些都是如此。

sentences.en: And I think kind of the most salient example I have from my book is in the runner-up chapter in job therapy.
sentences.zh: 我认为我在书中举出的最显著的例子是在“工作疗法”的候补章节中。

sentences.en: I think 7% of people are explicitly told why they were passed up for a promotion or raise.
sentences.zh: 我想只有7%的人被明确告知他们为什么没有获得晋升或加薪。

sentences.en: Most of them had to guess.
sentences.zh: 他们大多只能靠猜。

sentences.en: And that is a huge communication gap.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的沟通鸿沟。

sentences.en: Whose fault is that?
sentences.zh: 这是谁的错？

sentences.en: It's probably both people's fault.
sentences.zh: 可能是两个人的错。

sentences.en: But I don't think it just comes down to one conversation you have at work.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为这仅仅归结于你在工作中进行的一次谈话：

sentences.en: Why didn't I get promoted?
sentences.zh: 为什么我没有得到晋升？

sentences.en: It comes down to a thousand small conversations you didn't have at work around what you're doing potentially right or wrong.
sentences.zh: 它归结于你在工作中没有进行的成千上万次小对话，关于你可能做对了或做错了什么。

sentences.en: So I think a lot of us underestimate the power of those small daily organic conversations we have in helping us network and helping us figure out,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们很多人都低估了那些日常的小型、自然对话的力量，它们能帮助我们建立人脉，帮助我们弄清楚

sentences.en: how to troubleshoot and how to move forward.
sentences.zh: 如何解决问题以及如何前进。

sentences.en: And before you know it, 20 years in, you just can't manage to get that next step up and you have no idea why.
sentences.zh: 不知不觉中，20年过去了，你就是无法迈出下一步，而你完全不知道为什么。

sentences.en: And that's probably why.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是原因所在。

sentences.en: And that's something that I think most of us underestimate.
sentences.zh: 这是我们大多数人都低估的事情。

sentences.en: So just to wrap up, I like to ask this question sometimes to close.
sentences.zh: 所以总结一下，我有时喜欢用这个问题来收尾。

sentences.en: What are you working on?
sentences.zh: 你在研究什么？

sentences.en: What are the next big questions you're trying to answer?
sentences.zh: 你试图解答的下一个重大问题是什么？

sentences.en: What's your next book?
sentences.zh: 你的下一本书是什么？

sentences.en: Ooh.
sentences.zh: 噢。

sentences.en: I lay a lot on you.
sentences.zh: 你抛给我好多问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, my lab is doing some really fascinating research of what happens when we work with people who we disagree with politically and who are moral violators.
sentences.zh: 我的实验室正在做一些非常迷人的研究，关于当我们与政见不同且违背道德底线的人一起工作时会发生什么。

sentences.en: And I think one thing that's fascinating is looking at the difference between what people will say they'll do and what they actually do.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中一个迷人的地方在于，研究人们嘴上说会做的事与他们实际所做的事之间的差异。

sentences.en: And we're finding that a lot of us interact with people who we morally disagree with, politically disagree with.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，我们许多人都在与那些在道德和政治上与我们意见相左的人互动。

sentences.en: And we think that we're going to be pretty blunt in those interactions.
sentences.zh: 我们以为自己在这些互动中会相当直率。

sentences.en: But what we're finding is the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但我们发现恰恰相反。

sentences.en: The more immoral the person you're negotiating with, the nicer you are to them, the more likely you are to let them win that negotiation.
sentences.zh: 与你谈判的人越是不道德，你对他就会越好，你也就越有可能让他们赢得那场谈判。

sentences.en: And so some of these kinds of ironic effects of complex social processes that can shape us at work in ways that we often aren't thinking about so much.
sentences.zh: 因此，复杂社会过程会以我们往往没有想到的方式在工作中塑造我们，这产生了一些讽刺的效果。

sentences.en: I want to also do a lot work on anxious leadership.
sentences.zh: 我还想对焦虑型领导力做大量研究。

sentences.en: I mentioned in this podcast, the APA has done a lot of work on documenting the levels of stress and negative wellbeing among millennial leaders, among Gen Zers
sentences.zh: 我在这个播客中提到过，美国心理学协会（APA）做了大量工作来记录千禧一代领导者中的压力和消极幸福感水平，以及

sentences.en: who are being led by those millennial leaders, and what the dynamic impacts are to have this whole
sentences.zh: 由这些千禧一代领导者领导的Z世代员工的情况，以及拥有整整一代

sentences.en: generation of anxious leaders ushering in anxious direct reports and how that is then going to play out
sentences.zh: 焦虑领导者带领焦虑下属的动态影响，以及这将如何在

sentences.en: in the workplace, you know, to contrast them with baby boomers who are not anxious, who are direct communicators.
sentences.zh: 职场中表现出来，你知道的，以此来对比那些不焦虑、善于直接沟通的婴儿潮一代。

sentences.en: What is that going to do for performance, for growth, for, you know, all of these kinds of complex processes?
sentences.zh: 这对绩效、成长以及所有这些复杂的社会过程意味着什么？

sentences.en: So looking at some of those cohort effects that we had talked about earlier.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们要研究我们之前讨论过的一些同龄人群体效应。

sentences.en: So those are some of the projects that I'm thinking about right now.
sentences.zh: 这些就是我目前正在思考的一些项目。

sentences.en: Well, that's all really interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些真的都非常有趣。

sentences.en: I look forward to seeing more of your research.
sentences.zh: 我期待看到你更多的工作成果。

sentences.en: I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢你今天能来。

sentences.en: It's been very edifying.
sentences.zh: 这次谈话非常有启发性。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me on the show.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我参加这个节目。
